TL;DR

Welcome back to Dev Opportunity Radar.

This is a weekly series where I share opportunities, resources, communities, and interesting finds that I come across, with the goal of helping people discover things they might otherwise miss.

This week's edition features The Bridge by Entrepreneurs First, the Frontier AI Security Residency, the Figma Campus Leader Program 2026–2027, and The Missing Semester of Your CS Education, a free MIT course on the tools, workflows, and developer skills that every programmer should know.

If you're new to the series, you can now browse previous editions, search past opportunities, and explore Community Finds and Reader Updates on the Dev Opportunity Radar website. I've also written a short post about why I built it. You'll find links to both at the end of this article.

If you've discovered something through the radar, I'd love to hear about it. Whether you applied to an opportunity, joined a community, or found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd be happy to feature your experience in a future 💙 Reader Updates section (with your permission).

And if you've come across an opportunity, resource, community, program, or event that deserves more attention, feel free to share it in the comments.

If I feature one of your Community Finds in a future edition, I'll always make sure to credit you. If you discovered it, that recognition belongs to you.

📍 This Week's Opportunities

Here are a few opportunities I came across this week that I thought were worth sharing.

📌 The Bridge by Entrepreneurs First

Who it's for: Ambitious founders, engineers, researchers, product builders, and future startup CEOs based outside the US who want to build a venture-scale company. You don't need to have a co-founder or even a startup idea before applying.

What stands out: The Bridge is an 8-week, fully funded residency in San Francisco designed for exceptional international founders at the very beginning of their startup journey. Participants live and build together, explore ideas, meet potential co-founders, talk to users, and receive hands-on support from the Entrepreneurs First team.

I wanted to include this because most founder programs expect you to already have a company, traction, or a complete founding team. The Bridge is different. It's designed for people who are still figuring out what to build and who to build it with, while giving them the environment and support to make meaningful progress.

Another thing I like is that the residency is only the beginning. At the end of the eight weeks, teams that demonstrate strong potential can pitch to EF's Investment Committee. Selected teams receive a $250,000 pre-seed investment (in exchange for equity) and continue building in San Francisco for another three months with ongoing support from the EF team.

Duration: 8-week residency (plus an additional 3-month company-building program for funded teams)

Location: San Francisco, California

Cost: Free (housing, workspace, food, and the program are covered)

Who can apply: Exceptional founders based outside the US. You don't need an idea or a co-founder to apply.

Application Deadline: August 30, 2026

🔗 Learn More | 🔗 Apply

📌 Frontier AI Security Residency

Who it's for: Security engineers, cybersecurity professionals, hardware and embedded systems specialists, cryptography researchers, AI safety practitioners, and experienced software engineers interested in securing frontier AI systems. Prior research experience is helpful but not required, though the applied track generally expects around five or more years of industry experience.

What stands out: The Frontier AI Security Residency (FASR) is an 8-week, fully funded, in-person research and engineering residency in Cambridge, UK, run by ERA. Residents work on real-world challenges at the intersection of AI security, cybersecurity, and hardware verification, tackling problems such as securing frontier AI systems, verifying AI compute, and building mechanisms that make AI systems more trustworthy and verifiable.

I wanted to include this because most AI programs focus on building more capable models. This residency focuses on something just as important but discussed far less often: making advanced AI systems secure, verifiable, and resilient before their capabilities outpace our ability to protect them. If you're interested in the security side of AI rather than model development, opportunities like this are still relatively rare.

Another thing I like is how comprehensive the support is. The residency covers travel, accommodation, visas, workspace, and meals during working hours, pairs each resident with an experienced mentor and a Research Manager, and culminates in a research symposium where participants present their work. Residents also receive a pro-rated salary (based on an annual rate of £34,125), making it possible to focus entirely on the research without worrying about day-to-day expenses.

Duration: 8 weeks (October 12 – December 4, 2026)

Location: Cambridge, UK (primarily in person)

Funding: Fully funded, including travel, accommodation, visa support, workspace, and meals during working hours. Residents also receive a pro-rated salary.

Who can apply: Applicants worldwide aged 18 or older. The program values demonstrated technical ability over formal credentials. Prior research experience is not required, although the applied track generally expects experienced professionals.

Application Deadline: August 2, 2026

🔗 Learn More | 🔗 Apply

📌 Figma Campus Leader Program 2026–2027

Who it's for: University and college students in the United States, Canada, and India who have at least one academic year remaining, actively use Figma, and enjoy building communities around design, creativity, and product development. Students from any major are welcome.

What stands out: The Figma Campus Leader Program gives students the opportunity to become the official Figma ambassadors at their university. Campus Leaders work with the Figma for Education team to grow their campus design community by hosting workshops, events, and creative programs while helping other students learn and use Figma.

I wanted to include this because it's more than a typical campus ambassador program. Rather than focusing on promotion alone, it gives students the resources to build a lasting design community at their university while developing leadership, event planning, and community-building experience that carries well beyond college.

Another thing I like is that India is joining the program for the first time this year, making this a great opportunity for Indian students who previously weren't eligible. Campus Leaders also receive a community budget for events, exclusive mentorship and training, direct access to the Figma team, custom Figma swag, and a complimentary ticket to Config, Figma's annual conference for product builders.

Program Duration: August 2026 – June 2027

Time Commitment: Approximately 2–5 hours per week

Benefits: Community budget, Config ticket, exclusive swag, mentorship, portfolio reviews, training workshops, and direct access to the Figma team.

Who can apply: Students in the United States, Canada, and India with at least one academic year remaining who are active Figma users and passionate about design, creativity, and community building.

Application Deadline: August 2, 2026 (11:59 PM PDT)

🔗 Learn More | 🔗 Apply

📚 Resources Worth Checking Out

Not every useful find comes with an application deadline.

Here's one resource worth checking out this week.

The Missing Semester of Your CS Education

Who it's for: Computer science students, self-taught developers, early-career software engineers, and anyone who wants to become more confident with the tools they use every day while building software.

What stands out: Every computer science degree teaches things like algorithms, operating systems, databases, and programming languages. But very few teach you how to use the tools you'll spend hours with every single day. That's exactly what The Missing Semester of Your CS Education, created by instructors at MIT, is all about. Instead of focusing on another programming language or framework, the course covers practical topics like the command line, Git, debugging, development environments, SSH, code quality, documentation, packaging, and modern AI-assisted development workflows.

I wanted to include this because I think it's one of those resources that's easy to overlook. We spend so much time trying to learn the latest framework, library, or AI tool that we sometimes forget the skills that make us more productive no matter what we're building.

One thing I really liked is how practical the course is. It's full of the little things experienced developers often take for granted but that can make a huge difference once you learn them. If you've ever wondered how someone is so fast with Git, the terminal, debugging, or navigating a large codebase, there's a good chance they've picked up many of the skills this course teaches.

I also like that the course has continued to evolve alongside the software industry. The latest edition introduces Agentic Coding and naturally incorporates AI-assisted development throughout the lectures, while still emphasizing the fundamentals that every developer should know.

Topics Covered: Shell, development environments, debugging, Git, packaging, code quality, AI-assisted development, documentation, and more.

Cost: Free

Format: Online lectures, notes, and exercises

🌟 Community Finds

One of my favorite things about this series has been seeing people share opportunities, communities, and resources that others might not have discovered otherwise.

CALEC Volunteer and Internship Opportunities

Back in Edition #6, I featured CALEC's remote volunteer and internship opportunities after Francis (@francistrdev) shared them with the community. If you missed it, you can find the full overview and all the details in Edition #6.

Since sharing this opportunity with the community, Francis has also published a dedicated DEV post about the Full-Stack Developer volunteer role at CALEC. If that role interests you, it's worth checking out for his perspective and some additional information about what the team is looking for.

🔗 CALEC Volunteer & Internship Opportunities | 🔗 Edition #6

Thank you to Francis (@francistrdev) for thinking of the radar and sharing this with the community. It really means a lot 💙

I'd love for this section to keep growing.

If you've come across an opportunity, fellowship, grant, hackathon, conference, community, resource, or anything else you think more people should know about, feel free to share it in the comments.

If I feature it in a future edition, I'll always make sure to credit you. If you discovered it, that recognition belongs to you.

One small request: If you're sharing an opportunity, please avoid posting raw URLs directly in the comments. DEV sometimes filters them before I get a chance to see them.

A short description alongside the link makes it much easier for me to review and potentially feature it in a future edition.

💙 Reader Updates

One of my favorite parts of this series is seeing where the opportunities end up. This section is all about celebrating those stories.

⭐ This Week's Reader Spotlight

One of my favorite moments this week came from @anhmtk, who shared that they discovered OpenAI Build Week through Dev Opportunity Radar and were able to submit before the deadline.

They built AgentShare Live-Tester for the Developer Tools track, an OpenClaw workspace agent, and even shared one of the biggest lessons they learned while building. They found that Prompt Caching becomes much more cost-effective once the static prompt exceeds roughly 1,024 tokens, making autonomous agent workflows much cheaper to run.

If you're curious about what they built, you can also check out their Devpost submission.

Seeing readers discover an opportunity, build something, and then come back to share what they learned is exactly what I hoped this series would become.

I always enjoy when readers come back to share not just what they built, but what they learned along the way. Those little lessons often end up helping other developers too.

Thank you, @anhmtk, for sharing your journey and for letting me feature it here. Wishing you the very best with the judging. I'll be rooting for you!

💬 Share Your Story

I'd love for this section to keep growing over time.

If you discovered an opportunity through Dev Opportunity Radar, applied to something, joined a community, attended an event, or simply found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd genuinely love to hear about it.

You don't need to have been accepted or have a big success story to share. Sometimes simply discovering the right opportunity at the right time is already a win.

If you'd like to share an update, feel free to leave a comment on this edition. With your permission, I may feature it in a future 💙 Reader Updates section and tag you so other readers can celebrate your journey too.

I hope this section gradually becomes a place where we can celebrate those stories together, one update at a time.

👋 Until Next Friday

Before I go, I just want to say thank you.

Every week, I spend time searching for opportunities, resources, and communities that I think deserve a little more attention. But one of my favorite parts of this series isn't the research. It's seeing what happens after an edition is published.

Seeing someone discover an opportunity, apply to a program, share a resource, suggest a Community Find, or come back to tell us what they learned reminds me why I started Dev Opportunity Radar in the first place.

The goal has always been simple:

Help people discover opportunities they otherwise might have missed.

Thanks to all of you, it feels like we're doing exactly that.

Whether you've been reading since the very first edition or this is your first time here, thank you for being part of the journey. Every comment, suggestion, and shared opportunity helps make this series better than I could build on my own.

If you ever come across an opportunity, resource, event, community, or anything else you think deserves more attention, I'd love for you to share it in the comments. And if Dev Opportunity Radar helped you discover something exciting, I'd love to hear that too.

Thank you for reading, for sharing, and for helping make this our radar, not just mine.

I'll be back next Friday with more opportunities, resources, and Community Finds.

Until then, take care, and I hope you discover something amazing this week 💙

blocks.html_en: Who it's for: Ambitious founders, engineers, researchers, product builders, and future startup CEOs based outside the US who want to build a venture-scale company. You don't need to have a co-founder or even a startup idea before applying.

sentences.en: Who it's for: Ambitious founders, engineers, researchers, product builders, and future startup CEOs based outside the US who want to build a venture-scale company.
sentences.zh: 适合对象：雄心勃勃的创始人、工程师、研究人员、产品构建者以及美国境外想要建立风险投资规模公司的未来初创公司首席执行官。

sentences.en: You don't need to have a co-founder or even a startup idea before applying.

blocks.html_en: What stands out: The Bridge is an 8-week, fully funded residency in San Francisco designed for exceptional international founders at the very beginning of their startup journey. Participants live and build together, explore ideas, meet potential co-founders, talk to users, and receive hands-on support from the Entrepreneurs First team.

sentences.en: Participants live and build together, explore ideas, meet potential co-founders, talk to users, and receive hands-on support from the Entrepreneurs First team.

blocks.html_en: I wanted to include this because most founder programs expect you to already have a company, traction, or a complete founding team. The Bridge is different. It's designed for people who are still figuring out what to build and who to build it with, while giving them the environment and support to make meaningful progress.

📍本周的机会

以下是我本周遇到的一些我认为值得分享的机会。

📌 企业家优先的桥梁

适合对象：雄心勃勃的创始人、工程师、研究人员、产品构建者以及美国境外想要建立风险投资规模公司的未来初创公司首席执行官。 在申请之前，您不需要有联合创始人，甚至不需要有创业想法。

亮点：The Bridge 是一项为期 8 周、资金充足的旧金山驻地项目，专为刚开始创业之旅的杰出国际创始人而设计。 参与者一起生活、共同建设、探索想法、会见潜在的联合创始人、与用户交谈，并获得 Entrepreneurs First 团队的实际支持。

我想把这一点包括在内，因为大多数创始人计划都希望你已经拥有一家公司、牵引力或完整的创始团队。 大桥则不同。 它专为那些仍在弄清楚要构建什么以及与谁一起构建的人们而设计，同时为他们提供环境和支持以取得有意义的进展。

我喜欢的另一件事是，驻地只是一个开始。 八周结束时，表现出强大潜力的团队可以向 EF 投资委员会进行推介。 选定的团队将获得 250,000 美元的种子前投资（以换取股权），并在 EF 团队的持续支持下继续在旧金山进行为期三个月的建设。

持续时间：8 周驻留（加上为受资助团队提供的额外 3 个月的公司建设计划）

地点： 加利福尼亚州旧金山

费用：免费（涵盖住房、工作空间、食物和项目）

谁可以申请：美国境外的杰出创始人。 您不需要有想法或联合创始人即可申请。

申请截止日期：2026年8月30日

📌前沿人工智能安全驻场实习

适用人群：安全工程师、网络安全专业人员、硬件和嵌入式系统专家、密码学研究人员、人工智能安全从业者以及对保护前沿人工智能系统感兴趣的经验丰富的软件工程师。 先前的研究经验是有帮助的，但不是必需的，尽管应用轨道通常需要大约五年或更长的行业经验。

亮点：Frontier AI Security Residency (FASR) 是由 ERA 在英国剑桥举办的为期 8 周、资金充足的现场研究和工程实习项目。 居民致力于解决人工智能安全、网络安全和硬件验证交叉领域的现实挑战，解决诸如保护前沿人工智能系统、验证人工智能计算以及建立使人工智能系统更值得信赖和可验证的机制等问题。

我想包括这一点，因为大多数人工智能程序都专注于构建更强大的模型。 这次驻场培训重点关注同样重要但讨论较少的事情：在高级人工智能系统的能力超过我们保护它们的能力之前，使它们变得安全、可验证和有弹性。 如果您对人工智能的安全方面而不是模型开发感兴趣，那么这样的机会仍然相对较少。

我喜欢的另一件事是支持的全面性。 住院医师培训涵盖旅行、住宿、签证、工作空间和工作时间内的膳食，为每位住院医师配备一位经验丰富的导师和一名研究经理，并在研究研讨会上达到高潮，参与者在会上展示他们的工作。 居民还可以获得按比例计算的工资（基于年费 34,125 英镑），从而可以完全专注于研究，而不必担心日常开支。

持续时间：8周（2026年10月12日至12月4日）

地点：英国剑桥（主要亲自前往）

资金：全额资助，包括旅行、住宿、签证支持、工作空间和工作时间的膳食。 居民还可以获得按比例计算的工资。

谁可以申请：全世界年满 18 岁或以上的申请人。 该计划更看重展示的技术能力而不是正式的证书。 尽管应用轨道通常需要经验丰富的专业人士，但不需要先前的研究经验。

申请截止日期：2026 年 8 月 2 日

我想将其包括在内，因为它不仅仅是一个典型的校园大使计划。 它不仅仅专注于晋升，还为学生提供了在大学建立持久设计社区的资源，同时培养领导力、活动策划和社区建设经验，这些经验将远远超出大学的范围。

你计算机科学教育中缺失的一个学期

适合对象：计算机科学专业的学生、自学成才的开发人员、职业生涯早期的软件工程师以及任何想要对构建软件时日常使用的工具更加自信的人。

突出之处：每个计算机科学学位都会教授算法、操作系统、数据库和编程语言等内容。 但很少有人教你如何使用你每天要花几个小时使用的工具。 这正是由麻省理工学院的教师创建的《计算机科学教育中缺失的学期》的全部内容。 该课程不关注另一种编程语言或框架，而是涵盖命令行、Git、调试、开发环境、SSH、代码质量、文档、打包和现代人工智能辅助开发工作流程等实用主题。

我想将其包括在内，因为我认为这是很容易被忽视的资源之一。 我们花费大量时间尝试学习最新的框架、库或人工智能工具，以至于有时我们忘记了无论我们在构建什么，这些技能都可以让我们提高工作效率。

我真正喜欢的一件事是这门课程的实用性。 它充满了经验丰富的开发人员通常认为理所当然的小事情，但一旦你学会了它们，就会产生巨大的影响。 如果您曾经想知道为什么有人能够如此快速地使用 Git、终端、调试或浏览大型代码库，那么他们很可能已经掌握了本课程教授的许多技能。

我还喜欢该课程与软件行业一起不断发展。 最新版本介绍了代理编码，并在整个讲座中自然地融入了人工智能辅助开发，同时仍然强调每个开发人员都应该了解的基础知识。

涵盖的主题：Shell、开发环境、调试、Git、打包、代码质量、AI 辅助开发、文档等。

费用：免费

形式：在线讲座、笔记和练习
